title: The Last Bakery Revisited
premise: Beatrix Ashgrove has spent two decades hiding behind the counter of her bookshop, raising her daughter and avoiding the town's judgment after a fire that destroyed her family's bakery—and her reputation. When the local library's anonymous pen-pal program pairs her with gruff widower Elias Wren, the town's building inspector who once condemned the bakery ruins, their letters turn from hostile to tender before either realizes who's on the other end. As Beatrix fights to save the bakery site from demolition—a fight that would expose the truth that she started the fire as a desperate teenager—she must choose between protecting her secret and claiming a future with Elias. In the end, she confesses publicly, loses the building but gains forgiveness, and opens a small bakery corner inside her bookshop with Elias at her side.
about_author: H. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who spent fifteen years recommending romance novels to reluctant customers before writing one of her own. She lives in a coastal village where every street corner has a story, and most of them involve someone falling in love against their better judgment.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The librarian strong-arms Beatrix into the town's pen-pal program; she writes a guarded first letter, venting about the man trying to condemn her shop's crumbling annex—the old bakery ruins. Emotional beat: weary resistance to being seen.

chapters.title: Letters in the Dark
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias receives his assignment and recognizes nothing—Beatrix signs only 'B.' He writes back sharply about code violations, then softens when 'B' replies with unexpected wit. Emotional beat: curiosity cracking through professional armor.

chapters.title: Flour and Ash
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A flashback woven into present day: her daughter asks why they never bake together, forcing Beatrix to confront the sealed-off part of herself. She writes her pen-pal something almost honest. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing.

chapters.title: The Inspection
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias inspects the annex and finds structural failures he cannot ignore; he issues the condemnation notice, not knowing his correspondent owns it. They argue in person for the first time—sparks of hatred that feel suspiciously like chemistry. Emotional beat: duty colliding with attraction.

chapters.title: What B Never Said
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The letters grow intimate while daytime encounters grow hostile; both begin suspecting the truth. Beatrix realizes Elias was the young inspector who let her off with a warning twenty years ago. Emotional beat: dawning recognition and dread.

chapters.title: The Public Hearing
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the demolition hearing, Beatrix fights to save the annex without revealing why it matters so much. Elias testifies for safety, and the council votes to demolish. That night, an unsigned letter arrives at his office—she knows. Emotional beat: public defeat, private exposure.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Ruins
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confronts Beatrix in the ruined bakery; she confesses she started the fire as a teenager, fleeing an abusive home, and that he once showed her mercy without knowing it. He walks away shaken. Emotional beat: raw confession, devastating silence.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Mirror
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. With the annex condemned and Elias gone, Beatrix finally forgives the girl she was, telling her daughter the whole truth by the fire's old hearthstone. Her daughter suggests baking again—together. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness as the true climax.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias rereads every letter and realizes he fell for her honesty long before her name. He writes one final letter—signed this time—asking not for the past to be undone, but for a future built on truth. Emotional beat: vulnerable pursuit.

chapters.title: Rising Dough
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. On demolition day, Beatrix doesn't protest; instead she opens a tiny bakery corner inside the bookshop, flour on her hands for the first time in twenty years. Elias arrives with the last letter and stays. Emotional beat: love chosen freely, inheritance reclaimed in a new form.
